text: . Indian Railways recorded growth of 9 percent in freight loading in July this year as compared to the corresponding month of the previous year. It loaded 141.3 million tonnes of freight during July 2026, compared to 129.7 million tonnes in July last year. The performance reflects sustained demand across core sectors of the economy and continued efforts to improve freight logistics and operational efficiency.Further, Iron Ore loading increased by 22.2 per cent, Coal by 11.5 per cent, Food Grains by 11.5 per cent, Fertilizers by 12 per cent and Balance Other Goods by 12.1 per cent. Indian Railways stepped up domestic coal supply to power plants by 20 percent due to an increase in coal demand at thermal power plants, in July compared to the corresponding month last year.The increase in freight movement resulted in an incremental freight revenue of over one thousand one hundred crore rupees in July 2025, registering an 8 per cent growth. Additionally, Indian Railways carried 63.35 crore passengers during July 2026, compared to 62.19 crore during the corresponding month last year. Passenger traffic continued to grow across both suburban and non-suburban segments, reflecting the growing preference for rail travel across the country.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal met Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Laziz Kudratov in New Delhi today.  In a social media post, Mr Goyal said that during their meeting, they had productive discussions on further strengthening the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership by enhancing cooperation in trade, investment, pharmaceuticals, connectivity, digital technologies and manufacturing. Mr Goyal expressed confidence that the growing partnership between the two nations will unlock new opportunities for businesses and contribute to shared prosperity.

. The 2026 Commonwealth Games will come to a close with a spectacular closing ceremony at the iconic Hydro Arena in Glasgow tonight. The ceremony will begin at 1:30 am Indian Standard Time and will celebrate eleven days of sporting excellence, friendship and cultural diversity. On the occasion, Ahmedabad will receive the Commonwealth Games flag and the Host Baton in a ceremonial handover during the closing ceremony, marking India as the host for the centenary 2030 edition.India’s impressive campaign at the Games, highlighted by a record-breaking performance in boxing, historic success in judo, milestone achievements in para sports and multiple medals in athletics, propelled the country to fourth place in the overall medal standings with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze medals.The closing ceremony at Glasgow’s famous Hydro arena, which holds up to 13,000 fans, will bring eleven days of athletic competition to a finale. The event, which is primarily a celebration of athlete performances, also acts as a thank you to the numerous volunteers and presents the hosts for the last time with performances by cultural organizations and community groups. The official transfer to the 24th Commonwealth Games in Amdavad in 2030 will also take place during the event.The event will be headlined by Scottish rock band Simple Minds. BEMZ, Cammy Barnes and Sandi Thom will also perform, while Australian singer Delta Goodrem will be making her third appearance at a Commonwealth Games ceremony. From India, Rashmika Mandanna and Shankar Mahadevan will headline India’s cultural showcase in Glasgow. Doordarshan will broadcast the ceremony LIVE for the fans.

. The Supreme Court has directed the Reserve Bank of India to prepare and circulate a standard operating procedure (SOP) for dealing with mule accounts and bank accounts linked to cyber fraud. The court also issued a series of directions to states, Union Territories, law enforcement agencies and banks to strengthen grievance redressal, speed up the restoration of defrauded money and improve the handling of digital fraud cases.The apex court asked the RBI to provide copies of the SOP to the Registrars General of all high courts and directed states, Union Territories and law enforcement agencies to ensure the expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules. The court also directed states and Union Territories to operationalise the grievance redressal and money restoration modules and take steps to create public awareness about them. It asked the Registrars General of all high courts to apprise subordinate courts of the availability of the modules.The court sought a state-wise and bank-wise report on grievances registered and resolved, directed authorities to expedite cases involving frozen bank accounts, and asked the Inter-Departmental Committee to consult banks and intermediaries on preventing digital arrest scams and recovering defrauded money.In another decision, Supreme Court directed the central government to develop a pilot project linking fuel sales to valid third-party motor insurance, proposing that uninsured vehicles be denied fuel at petrol pumps until coverage is obtained. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra said nearly 56 percent of vehicles on Indian roads are uninsured and called the situation shocking.The court directed the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India and the Centre to pilot Automatic Number Plate Recognition, ANPR-based insurance verification to identify uninsured vehicles and improve compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act.

. The Ministry of Education today opened the online registration portal for Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat initiative. The Ministry said that interested youth aged between 18 and 30 years, including students of Higher Education Institutions, NSS/NYKS volunteers, and young professionals, are eligible to register. It said that for Phase VII, 20 Higher Education Institutions including IITs, IIMs, Central Universities and NITs have been identified as nodal institutions to host and facilitate the exchange programme. Selected participants will undertake five to seven day educational and cultural tours to their paired States and Union Territories. They will gain first-hand exposure to local traditions, educational institutions, governance initiatives, innovation ecosystems, industries, heritage sites, and community life during the exchange programme.

. India’s coal production has witnessed a growth of 7.51 percent in July 2026, compared to the same period last year. The Ministry of Coal informed that the overall coal production in the country during July this year has reached 69.75 million tonnes as per provisional data. It added that the coal dispatch during the last month showed a growth of 17.34 percent year on year in July. The cumulative coal production up to July, in financial year 2026-27 stood at 302.24 million tonnes (Provisional), while the cumulative coal dispatch reached 354.70 million tonnes (Provisional), registering a growth of 5.87 percent over the same period of last Financial Year.

. The Parliament has passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, with Rajya Sabha approving it today. Lok Sabha has already passed the Bill. Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai moved the bill, which aims to amend the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.The new bill has been brought to make provisions for delayed registration more stringent and to encourage timely reporting of events of birth and death. The Bill provides that if a birth or death is reported to the Registrar more than one year but within two years after its occurrence, it may be registered only with the approval of the District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate, or an Executive Magistrate authorised by the District Magistrate, following verification of the authenticity of the birth or death.Replying to debate over the Bill, Mr Rai said, the bill has been brought in view of the possible misuse of delayed registration. He said, if a birth or death is reported to the Registrar more than two years, it will be registered only on the order of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class. The Minister said, the system remains largely unchanged, except for the provision of delayed registration beyond two years.Mr Rai said that the intent behind this amendment is clear as the government wants to ensure that every child born in the country is duly registered. The Minister added that it also aims to prevent discrepancies such as cases where births are registered improperly or manipulated for vested interests. He said, similarly, every death must also be properly recorded in a timely manner, ensuring that there is no scope for misuse or irregularities in records.The Minister noted that nearly 3.5 lakh registration units are functioning across the country. Mr Rai stated that birth registration in the country, which was around 86.6 per cent in 2014, has increased to over 99 per cent in 2024. Similarly, death registration, which was around 72.5 per cent, has now risen to 99.4 per cent. He said India is progressing with confidence towards achieving universal and accurate birth and death registration.Earlier, participating in the discussion, BJP’s Darshana Singh said that the registration of births and deaths is not merely an administrative process but an important document of identity for every citizen. She stated that this Bill has been introduced to make the system simpler, transparent, and effective in line with the changing times. Ms Singh said that the birth and death registration system has been digitized, which will help make records secure and reliable. She added that India has made remarkable progress in the field of birth and death registration. She emphasized that in recent years, significant progress has been made toward making citizen services more transparent and technology-driven.BJD member Dr Santrupt Misra expressed concern over the provision in the Bill that requires such matters to be referred to a First Class Judicial Magistrate after a period of two years. He said that courts are already burdened with a large number of cases and there is no need to involve a First Class Judicial Magistrate.Meda Raghunadha Reddy of YSRCP, said that his Party supports every effort to strengthen the integrity of India’s civil registration system and to prevent identity fraud. He said, India’s civil registration system has made remarkable progress over the years. He said, before 2000, only about 56 per cent of births and 48 per cent of deaths were registered nationally. Mr Reddy added that a reliable civil registration system is essential not only for legal identity but also for effective governance, policy planning, and the delivery of public services. Phulo Devi Netam of Congress, Mamata Thakur of TMC, Ravi Chandra Vaddiraju of BRS and M Dhanapal of AIADMK, among others, participated in the discussion.After the passage of the Bill, the Rajya Sabha was adjourned till 11 AM tomorrow.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by four paise to end at 95 rupees and 38 paise against the US dollar.

. The Government has refuted claims circulating on social media that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has announced free electric bicycles for students having their Aadhaar card. The Fact-Check Unit of Press Information Bureau has said that the video is fake and digitally manipulated. It said that the Prime Minister has not made any such announcement. It has urged people to report such suspicious content to the Government.

. Former champion PV Sindhu will be the ninth seed in the women’s singles event at the BWF World Badminton Championships 2026, scheduled to be held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi from August 17 to 23. India’s highest-seeded entry at the World Badminton Championships will be the men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have been handed the fifth seed. Former world championships bronze medallist Lakshya Sen is seeded 14th in men’s singles, while Dhruv Kapila and Olympian Tanisha Crasto are the 15th seeds in mixed doubles. India will have two entries in each of the five badminton disciplines at the home world championships, with at least one seeded contender in four of them.

. Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that sustained institutional reforms, technology-driven governance and continuous monitoring have significantly strengthened the country’s vigilance framework. The minister said this during his meeting with the outgoing Central Vigilance Commissioner, Praveen Kumar Srivastava. Dr Singh said that the framework has led to a sharp reduction in the pendency of disciplinary cases from over 4000 to nearly 700 in about three to four years. He noted that transparent and time-bound vigilance mechanisms are essential for good governance and inspire greater public confidence in institutions. He said that the significant reduction in pending disciplinary cases demonstrates the impact of sustained administrative reforms and closer coordination among Ministries, Departments and vigilance authorities.Mr Srivastava also briefed the Minister on the major initiatives undertaken by the Central Vigilance Commission in recent years to modernise vigilance administration through technology, process reforms and capacity building. The meeting reviewed the Commission’s increasing emphasis on technology-enabled vigilance through initiatives relating to digital governance, fraud prevention in banking and financial institutions, cyber security and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence.

. Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh, is hosting an important BRICS cultural meeting from today. Delegates from several countries have arrived in the city for four days of discussions on culture.The four-day event, being held under India’s BRICS Presidency, will continue till the 8th of August. It includes meetings of the BRICS Culture Working Group and the BRICS Culture Ministers. The city has been specially decorated for the event. VIP Road and Bhoj Setu have been beautified with fresh paint and murals.The first two days are for discussions among senior officials. The last two days will have meetings of Culture Ministers, who will finalise a joint declaration. India has placed two important proposals before the member countries. One is to create a shared digital platform for artists and cultural heritage. The second is to encourage joint UNESCO nominations by BRICS nations.

. Global crude oil prices dropped today. Brent crude was trading 2.6 per cent down at 81 US dollars and 57 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 3.3 per cent lower at 77 US dollars and 65 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meeting will be held from today till August 7 in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The Education Ministry said that these meetings will bring together education ministers, senior officials and delegates from BRICS member countries.During the meeting, they will deliberate on the topics of collaboration, including the following priority areas such as strengthening early childhood care and education, strengthening skill development and enhanced cooperation and promoting collaborative research, innovation and start-ups. Union Education Minister Prahlad Joshi will participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched the revamped version of TRAI MyCall, a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. TRAI MyCall is a citizen-centric digital platform that empowers telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, along with relevant network parameters. The platform also strengthens evidence-based regulatory oversight by enabling TRAI to assess the Quality of Experience across telecom networks based on real consumer feedback. TRAI MyCall application can be installed on Android devices from https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.trai.my

. The legal team representing Bangladeshi Hindu monk Chinmoy Krishna Das has voiced deep concern over the deliberate pacing of his release process. Chinmoy Krishna Das, a leading spokesperson for Bangladesh’s Sanatani Hindu community, was arrested at Dhaka’s Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on November 25, 2024, on sedition charges. His arrest triggered widespread agitation across the country, culminating in violent clashes between security personnel and his supporters outside the Chattogram Court Building on 27th November, 2024.Speaking to a news agency, Chinmoy Das’s defence attorney, Apurba Kumar Bhattacharjee, said, the state mechanism has repeatedly stacked charges to prolong his incarceration. He said, despite securing bail in the original sedition charge and several subsequent cases, a web of fresh charges continues to keep the minority rights advocate behind bars.

. Young cyclist Harshita Jakhar rode into history books by becoming the first Indian woman to be a part of the Tour de France Femmes in Switzerland. The 19-year-old led a pack of eight talented cyclists from Afghanistan, Algeria, Chile, Ethiopia with two riders, Namibia and Uganda during the ceremonial start at Stage 2 of the gruelling race yesterday. The event started on 1st of this month in Lausanne and will end on 9th August in Nice.The team, handpicked by UCI (Union Cycliste de Internationale), cycled 4.5 kilometres on a neutralised section of the course along with some riders from the WCC Road Team.Tour de France Femmes is the women’s multi-stage cycling race that corresponds to the men’s Tour de France. It is part of the UCI Women’s World Tour calendar.UCI President David Lappartient joined the riders on the start podium before the stage and expressed his delight at seeing an Indian in the mix.Hailing from Rajasthan, Harshita has been making waves on the Indian cycling circuit, sweeping almost all the medals on offer in junior category and winning regularly in the seniors section as well. Her aim is to finish among the Top 10 at the 2026 Asian Games, and win a medal in the 2030 Games.

. In Badminton, unseeded Indian pair Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy upset sixth seeds Chaloempon Charoenkitamorn and Worrapol Thongsa-Nga of Thailand 21-16, 21-18 to advance to the men’s doubles second round at the Korea Masters tournament in Asan today.However, India’s other men’s doubles pair, Achutaditya Rao Doddavarapu and Arjun Reddy Pochana, lost 3-21, 10-21 to second seeds Choi Sol Gyu of Korea and Goh V Shem of Malaysia.In women’s doubles, Priya Konjengbam and Shruti Mishra went down 15-21, 13-21 to Japan’s second-seeded pair Ririna Hiramoto and Kokona Ishikawa.

. In badminton, Isharani Baruah defeated South Korean Lee So Hee 18-21, 21-15, 7-21 in the quarter-finals at the Korea Masters Super 300 badminton tournament in Asan today.India’s top shuttlers, including reigning Taipei Open women’s singles champion Tanvi Sharma and former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth, will begin their campaigns.In the men’s singles category, Kiran George, Rounak Chouhan, Saneeth Dayanand and Tharun Mannepalli are among the Indian players in action, while Anmol Khar, Malvika Bansod, and Aakarshi Kashyap will represent India in the women’s singles category. However, India endured a mixed start to the competition on the opening day.Unseeded Indian pair Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy upset sixth seeds Chaloempon Charoenkitamorn and Worrapol Thongsa-Nga of Thailand 21-16, 21-18 to enter the men’s doubles second round at the Korea Masters Super 300 badminton tournament in Asan, South Korea,In men’s doubles, Achutaditya Rao Doddavarapu and Arjun Reddy Pochana were eliminated in the first round. In women’s doubles, Priya Konjengbam and Shruti Mishra went down 15-21, 13-21 to Japan’s second-seeded pair Ririna Hiramoto and Kokona Ishikawa. In men’s singles qualifying, Tushar Suveer defeated Canada’s Shaurya Gullaiya 21-15, 21-12 before losing to Japan’s Shogo Ogawa 10-21, 17-21 in the next qualifying round.India has fielded a 33-member contingent across men’s singles, women’s singles, men’s doubles, women’s doubles and mixed doubles at the tournament.

. India has termed the so-called local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir a complete farce, saying such hollow exercises cannot hide reality. Briefing media in New Delhi, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal pointed out that the real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces.He said that since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown. He said that the Pakistani establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, black outs, intimidation and repression and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise. He added that Pakistan must be held accountable and the world should see through Pakistan’s hypocritical lecturing on human rights.Replying to a query on invitation for BRICS Summit to be held in Delhi in September, Mr Jaiswal said a formal invitation for a bilateral visit to India was extended to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman upon his assumption of office in February this year.He informed that as far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister in his capacity as the current Chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He added that the invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner.On a media interaction by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the spokesperson said that the interaction is being organised by a private media entity. He said the government has no involvement in it and neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum.

. As the unrest in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) continues to mount, the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) today alleged that Pakistani forces opened live fire and used tear gas against unarmed civilians in Bagh district. JAAC said this on a social media platform while sharing the ground footage.The allegations also include Pakistani forces setting civilians’ motorcycles ablaze in the Makri region of Muzaffarabad district in the occupied territory. These latest incidents came amid escalating brutality by Pakistani forces against protestors across PoJK, where over 50 people have reportedly been killed and hundreds injured over the past few days.

. At least eight people were killed after Ukraine launched a large-scale overnight drone attack targeting military, energy, and civilian infrastructure across several regions of Russia. According to Russia’s Defence Ministry, its air defence systems intercepted 635 drones during the attack. Local authorities said, three people were killed and two others injured in the Udmurtia region, while three more people lost their lives and five were injured in the Belgorod region. Two fatalities were reported in another area.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, Kyiv’s forces targeted a military airbase in Engels, which houses Russian long-range bombers, as well as an oil refinery in Saratov. Ukraine also claimed that its forces struck an oil depot in Russia’s western Kaluga region and reported fires at the targeted facilities.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in negative zone today, snapping a four-day gaining streak. The Sensex shed 210 points or nearly 0.3 percent to close at 78,429. The Nifty dropped 159 points or more than 0.6 percent to settle at 24,615.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 0.3 per cent while the Smallcap 100 index gained 0.2 percent.In the Sensex pack, 16 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top gainers, Trent rose as well as Bajaj Finance gained 1.1 per cent, Bharat Electronics Limited added 0.9 per cent and Tata Steel increased 0.6 per cent. In contrast, Hindustan Unilever fell 1.7 per cent, NTPC lost 1.6 per cent and HDFC Bank shed one and a half per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 19 outof 28 sectors ended in negative zone. Among the top underperformers, Insurance plunged 2.1 per cent, Realty as well as Housing Finance shed 1.2 per cent and Utilities dropped 0.6 per cent. In contrast, Capital Goods gained one per cent, Metal rose 0.9 per cent and Industrials added half a per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2028 companies declined, 2108 advanced, and 196 remained unchanged.

. Iran said today there were no talks under ​way with the United States and no plans for any meetings, contradicting U.S. President Donald Trump who had said that negotiations with Iran through intermediaries are scheduled to take place today. Speaking to reporters on board Air Force One, Mr. Trump had said that diplomatic engagements involving Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Iran led him to halt what was originally planned as a massive attack. However, Iran’s Foreign ⁠Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected the claim, saying no negotiations with the United States were taking place and no meetings were scheduled. Baghaei added that all Iranian negotiators were ​currently in the country, apart from Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, who was on a religious pilgrimage in Iraq. The only talks under way, he said, were discussions with Oman over management of the Strait of Hormuz.

. An Indian-flagged commercial vessel, MSV Faize Noore Oliya, sank in the Red Sea after coming under attack off the coast of Yemen yesterday. All the 14 seafarers, including 13 Indian nationals, who were on board the vessel were rescued safely. According to reports, the Indian-flagged tanker was carrying oil from Saudi Arabia.Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal said that the vessel was hit by a projectile near Yemeni waters, causing the vessel to capsize and sink. Mr Sonowal said, India strongly condemns this unprovoked attack on the defenceless mechanised sailing vessel. He said, the safety of our people is our supreme priority.In a statement, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) condemned the attack on the Indian-flagged vessel, saying the continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. It said the targeting of commercial shipping in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region must be restored at the earliest.The Ministry said that the Indian Embassy in Riyadh is closely monitoring the situation and proactively coordinating with Yemeni authorities for the safety and security of the crew.

. Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has dedicated India’s first indigenous MA-104 Cell Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine for pigs. The Ministry said that the vaccine is a major breakthrough in veterinary research and is well suited for large-scale production. It said that the vaccine has successfully undergone comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including sterility, purity, safety, genetic stability, immunogenicity, protective efficacy and virulence reversion studies. The vaccine was field validated in collaboration with the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying further establishing its safety and efficacy under field conditions. The vaccine is recommended for healthy pigs above eight weeks of age and is administered as a 1 mL intramuscular injection, followed by a booster dose 14 days after the primary vaccination. Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Rajiv Ranjan Singh was present on the occasion.Speaking on the development, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Dr. M.L. Jat said that this breakthrough marks the dawn of a new era in veterinary science. He said that the breakthrough reflects India’s growing scientific capability to develop world-class animal health solutions and paves the way for a new generation of indigenously developed vaccines.Over 1.5 lakh passenger journeys were recorded in a single day on the Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat on the 3rd of this month.

. The countdown to the 2030 Ahmedabad Commonwealth Games has officially begun, with the curtain falling on the Glasgow Commonwealth Games last night. As the curtain came down, India offered the world a vibrant invitation to Ahmedabad, blending ancient philosophy, contemporary artistry and cultural grandeur in a handover presentation that officially launched the journey towards the centenary edition of the Games in 2030.Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh, representing King Charles III, formally declared the Games closed in Glasgow. He called up on athletes of all countries and territories to visit Ahmedabad in four years’ time to celebrate the 24th Commonwealth Games.The formal handover began with the Commonwealth Games flag making its symbolic journey across the arena. Led by bearers holding the Scottish and Indian flags, the procession lowered the folded Games flag. Glasgow’s Lord Provost Jacqueline McLaren then passed it to Commonwealth Games Scotland vice-chair Susan Jackson, two-time Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, and finally Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi.This marked the official transfer of hosting responsibilities from Scotland to India. India last hosted the Commonwealth Games in New Delhi in 2010. After 11 days of intense competition, Indian athletes departed from Glasgow as a satisfied bunch after winning 39 medals at the 2026 Games, including 13 gold, 17 silver, and nine bronze, to end in fourth position on the standings.

. The Uttar Pradesh Government will provide free travel in State Roadways buses for women aged 60 years and above.In the First Supplementary Budget for the financial year 2026-27, a provision of rupees 100 crore has been made to reimburse the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation for implementing this initiative. The Bharatiya Janata Party had promised this measure in its Lok Kalyan Sankalp Patra. This decision will provide financial relief to millions of senior women across the state, enabling them to travel for religious, social, family, and healthcare-related needs.In addition, the government has allocated an additional rupees 1,094.40 crore to the Women Welfare Department, strengthening key schemes such as the Destitute Women Pension Scheme, the Mukhyamantri Bal Seva Yojana, and various programmes related to the protection of women and children. These provisions further reinforce the government’s commitment to women’s safety, dignity, social security, and economic empowerment. Sushil Chandra Tiwari, Aakashwani news, Lucknow.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today felicitated Indian athletes who returned from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after delivering historic performances in boxing, judo and para-athletics. During the felicitation ceremony held in New Delhi, the medal winners were presented cash awards of 30 lakh rupees for gold, 20 lakh rupees for silver and 10 lakh rupees for bronze.Interacting with the athletes, Dr. Mandaviya asked the athletes to think beyond their playing careers and become contributors to the next generation of Indian sport. The Minister highlighted the revamped Khelo India scheme of worth rupees 36,000 crore. He said that this initiative will take care of greater continued investment in the growth of Indian sports in the coming years. Congratulating the champions, Dr. Mandaviya urged them to extend their contribution to Indian sport beyond their competitive careers by mentoring and inspiring the next generation of athletes.

. Union Minister for Development of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya Scindia, today met Commonwealth Games gold medallist Mirabai Chanu in New Delhi and congratulated her on winning a record-extending third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow. During the meeting, Mr Scindia lauded Mirabai Chanu’s determination and perseverance, and noted that her achievement will inspire young athletes across the country, particularly in the Northeast. They also discussed various aspects of high-performance sports, including training, nutrition, recovery and athlete support.The Minister highlighted the Centre’s efforts to strengthen the sporting ecosystem in the Northeast through the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region’s High-Level Task Force and the One State, One Sport initiative. He said that the primary focus of the Government is to create world-class coaching, scientific training and sports infrastructure, nurturing more champions from the region.

. Protests by students over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examination have intensified in Jharkhand. Thousands of aspirants have been staging an indefinite protest for the past 12 days at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi.Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi has become a symbol of the anger and anguish of young aspirants protesting against the alleged irregularities in the JPSC examination. However, the protesters claim that despite braving the scorching sun and remaining at the protest site, they have been deprived of basic amenities such as drinking water, food and toilet facilities.Union Minister of State for Defence and Ranchi MP, Sanjay Seth, has criticised the Opposition for remaining silent on the issue. He alleged that the state government has shown complete insensitivity, claiming that no representative of the government has visited the protesting students so far.As the shortage of basic facilities at the protest site continues, Godda MP Nishikant Dubey has also targeted the Hemant Soren-led government. He has levelled serious allegations that seats in the examination were sold and questioned the government’s handling of the recruitment process.Describing the plight of the protesting students as a reflection of the state government’s insensitivity, former Chief Minister Arjun Munda said that the fight for the rights of the youth would not remain confined to Ranchi alone.With allegations of paper leak and lack of basic facilities at the protest site, the students say they are determined to continue their agitation. It remains to be seen how soon the administration responds to their demands.

. Premier pacer Jasprit Bumrah is set to miss India’s two-Test tour of Sri Lanka after failing to recover fully from a knee injury. The Sri Lanka series begins from 15th of this month in Galle.The swelling in Cricketer’s knee seems to be more serious than it initially looked, and the Sports Science team at Bengaluru’s Centre of Excellence doesn’t want to rush the seasoned pacer to the grind of international cricket, keeping in mind a packed calendar ahead.The 32-year-old had missed out on the third ODI against England at Lord’s after sustaining an impact injury.India are already dealing with several injury concerns, with Harshit Rana sidelined by a hamstring injury and Nitish Kumar Reddy due to a quadriceps injury. Washington Sundar has been ruled out of the first Test due to a hamstring injury, while Akash Deep remains unavailable as he continues his recovery from stress reactions in his back.The opening Test between India and Sri Lanka will be played at the Galle International Stadium from 15th August, while the second Test is scheduled in Colombo from 23rd August.The series will form part of the ongoing ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle. Led by Shubman Gill, India are currently fifth in the World Test Championship standings, having registered four wins and four losses in nine matches, with a Points Percentage (PCT) of 48.150.

. The Government has refuted claims circulating on social media of fuel adulteration or contamination. In a social media post, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas clarified that fuel quality is monitored on a regular basis by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs). It said that in addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets.The Ministry said that over two thousand samples have also been tested for chloride and sulphide, of which only 2 cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately. It said strict action will be taken in case any contamination or adulteration is found in any retail outlet. It informed that OMCs have also been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination in the entire fuel supply chain.
